title: Recursion
summary: A function that solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller piece, plus how to keep it fast.

sections.heading: A function that calls itself
body: Every recursive function needs two parts:
- A **base case**: a small input you can answer directly, which stops the calls.
- A **recursive step**: do a little work, then call yourself on a smaller input.

sections.heading: A natural fit for nested data
body: Lists inside lists, any number of levels deep, are hard to handle with plain loops. With recursion: if an item is a list, handle it the same way you handle the whole thing.

sections.heading: Remember answers you already worked out
body: Some recursive functions ask the same question again and again. `fib(50)` written plainly makes billions of calls.
Store each answer the first time you compute it (this is called memoization). The second time, look it up.

mistakes: No base case, or one that is never reached: you get "Maximum call stack size exceeded" or `RecursionError`.
Calling yourself with an input that is not smaller.
Forgetting to `return` the result of the recursive call.
